_why: THE ONE DECLARATION OF WHAT TEARDOWN MAY DESTROY. Read by scripts/sandbox.sh and by
adapters/domain/code's inspect_sandbox/close_sandbox. Issue #103: the script's own comment
said it 'mirrors inspect_sandbox()', and it mirrored the bug -- so the rule lives here, in
one file, rather than twice in two languages where it would drift.
THE QUESTION TEARDOWN ASKS IS NOT THE CHANGE-SET QUESTION. A change set asks what may be
applied; teardown asks whether anything here exists ONLY here. `git status --porcelain`
answers neither -- it omits ignored files entirely, so a sandbox whose only copy of some work
sits under an ordinary .gitignore reported dirty_files: 0 and safe_to_close: true.
THE DISTINCTION IS REPRODUCIBILITY, NOT TRACKED-NESS. An ignored build artifact can be
rebuilt; an ignored notes/ directory cannot. Everything ignored and NOT listed below counts
as unreproducible and blocks teardown. Adding an entry here is a claim that the path can be
regenerated from the source of record by a documented command -- state the command.
The 2026-09-13 run nearly lost 1400 authored lines to a sandbox believed empty, and was saved
only by inspect reporting dirty_files: 21. This list is what that check is worth.
PATHS MATCH AT ANY DEPTH. This is a pnpm workspace: dist/ and node_modules/ exist under
every package, so an entry here means that name wherever it appears, not only at the root.

reproducible.regenerated_by: pnpm run typecheck && pnpm run build
any turbo run; it is a cache
nothing regenerates a log; it is diagnostic, not work
the Finder; it is macOS metadata, never work
any python3 run; it is bytecode cache

_not_listed_on_purpose: state/artifacts -- retention classes live there; §7 makes SQLite the authoritative home for
control-plane history, and an artifact under a retention class is evidence, not scratch.
state/debug -- CLAUDE.md §8 permits rm -rf there, but permitting deletion is not the same as
claiming regeneration. A debug capture of a crash exists only once.
